originalTitle: Bessent's efforts in the Treasury market so far haven't worked. Here's what else he can try
summary: Market experts showed skepticism at whether the push would succeed against a bevy of factors working against Treasurys.
content:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent insisted Thursday that he has multiple weapons at his disposal to quell liquidity problems in the government debt market and restore calm.

While that's true in itself, a two-pronged effort he has deployed so far — accelerated buybacks and an effort to talk the market into accepting the rationale — have met with little success.

The Treasury announcement Wednesday that it would at least double its bond buybacks starting in early September sent yields tumbling as investors applauded a backstop for longer-maturity government bonds.

However, yields at the long end quickly rose again Thursday as market experts showed skepticism at whether the push would succeed against a bevy of factors working against Treasurys.

Then on Thursday, Bessent appeared on CNBC with assurances that the intervention was merely aimed at providing market liquidity and not at trying to control the yield curve. While yields initially nudged lower, they quickly rebounded amid criticism of how the prior day's announcement was rolled out, leading one analyst to characterize the appearance as having "minimal impact" on the market pressures.

Still, that leaves Bessent with a variety of options that he may yet choose to deploy.

"We have a big toolkit," the Treasury chief said. "Part of it is signaling here and to show that we believe that the yields don't reflect the underlying fundamentals."

Yet markets are still worried, and criticism rose that the size of the buybacks, which Bessent confirmed could exceed $4 billion, would be rendered ineffective in such a large market.

Evercore ISI analyst Krishna Guha called the plan "a weak form of Operation Twist," or a Federal Reserve initiative that swaps longer-term notes and bonds for short-term bills. The move "in itself will have little enduring impact and could backfire if it is seen as signaling concern about the ability to fund longer-term at acceptable cost," he said. The interview "had minimal impact on the bond market," he added.

That leaves Bessent with a handful of other options, none guaranteed to work and each carrying its own risk:

Whichever route he chooses — and he could also choose to do nothing and let the markets sort it out — Bessent could face credibility challenges from a market already growing skeptical and leery of the challenges Treasurys are facing.

Jefferies' chief U.S. economist, Thomas Simons, complained that the buyback announcement itself was improper. He pointed out that the move came two weeks after Treasury announced its quarterly refunding plans, during which it gave no indication that it was considering changing the buyback scheme.

"This breaks with Treasury's long-held strategy of making 'regular and predictable' announcements, and using the Refunding to announce almost all of their policy changes and guidance," Simons wrote. "We do not think it is hyperbole to say that this break in communication strategy reduces the overall credibility of their guidance."

Moreover, Simons added that "the sloppy wording of [the] headline on [the] release gave the impression that this was a hastily made decision."

The challenge, then, for Bessent could be that efforts to suppress longer-end yields could give investors another reason to demand more compensation.

Along the lines of what Bessent told CNBC on Thursday, not all of the factors at play are fundamental. They include rising competition from corporate bond issuance as well as suddenly attractive yields of other sovereigns including Japan; a correlation with oil prices that in turn increases inflation fears; and increasing term premiums, or the extra yield investors are demanding.

To combat those problems, Bessent could seek cooperation with the Federal Reserve. Though Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has stressed the importance of letting the market set rates, Bessent suggested Thursday that the two entities "would work together" in dealing with complications in the bond markets and as the central bank manages its own Treasury holdings.

The various moving parts come during a paradigm shift in the government debt markets, both in the U.S. and globally.

"There has also been a structural shift in who buys U.S. government debt," said Atsi Sheth, chief credit officer at Moody's Ratings. "As central banks shrink their balance sheets and traditional duration buyers reach the limits of how much additional issuance they can absorb, new buyers, such as leveraged hedge funds running relative-value strategies, are playing a bigger role."

On top of all that, the U.S. faces a daunting fiscal situation in the form of a deficit-to-GDP ratio of nearly 6%, or about triple its average from the end of World War II until the Covid pandemic. That is compounding a problem with the national debt , which just surpassed $40 trillion.

With President Donald Trump hungry for tax cuts and Congress showing few signs of spending restraint, the fiscal problems are likely to mount. To that end, Bessent said he and Russell Vought, head of the Office of Management and Budget, will meet soon to discuss "fiscal consolidation," generally understood to refer to efforts to reduce red ink.

"It's that combination of the deficits, the borrowing needs, inflation expectations, not really knowing what future Fed policy is going to be, and the sustainability of being able to issue higher, ever higher, levels of U.S. Treasury debt, and what rates those need to be at," said JoAnne Bianco, senior investment strategist at BondBloxx. "There's just the idea that there needs to be a higher risk premium for all the issuance."
chineseTitle: 迄今为止，贝森特在国债市场的努力尚未奏效。这是他还可以尝试的其他方法
chineseSummary: 由于一系列不利于美国国债的因素，市场专家对这一举措能否成功表示怀疑。
chineseContent:
美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特周四坚称，他拥有多种武器可以平息政府债务市场的流动性问题并恢复平静。

虽然这本身就是事实，但他迄今为止采取的双管齐下的努力——加速回购和努力说服市场接受这一理由——却收效甚微。

周三，财政部宣布将从 9 月初开始将债券回购规模至少增加一倍，这导致收益率暴跌，因为投资者对长期政府债券的支持表示欢迎。

然而，由于市场专家对一系列不利于美国国债的因素的推动是否会成功表示怀疑，周四长期债券收益率再次迅速上升。

周四，贝森特出现在 CNBC 节目中，并保证干预只是为了提供市场流动性，而不是试图控制收益率曲线。虽然收益率最初小幅走低，但由于前一天公告的发布方式受到批评，收益率迅速反弹，导致一位分析师将这一消息描述为对市场压力的“影响微乎其微”。

尽管如此，贝森特仍有多种选择可供选择。

“我们有一个很大的工具包，”财政部长说。 “其中一部分是在此发出信号，表明我们认为收益率并未反映潜在的基本面。”

然而市场仍然感到担忧，批评人士认为，贝森特确认的回购规模可能超过 40 亿美元，但在如此大的市场中，回购规模将变得无效。

Evercore ISI分析师克里希纳·古哈(Krishna Guha)称该计划是“扭曲行动的一种弱形式”，即美联储将长期票据和债券换成短期票据的举措。他表示，此举“本身不会产生持久影响，如果这被视为表明人们担心以可接受的成本进行长期融资的能力，则可能会适得其反”。他补充说，这次采访“对债券市场的影响微乎其微”。

这给 Bessent 留下了一些其他选择，但没有一个能保证有效，而且每个选择都有自己的风险：

无论他选择哪条路线——他也可以选择什么也不做，让市场来解决——市场已经对美国国债面临的挑战越来越持怀疑态度，贝森特可能会面临可信度挑战。

杰富瑞首席美国经济学家托马斯·西蒙斯抱怨说，回购公告本身就是不恰当的。他指出，此举是在财政部宣布季度退款计划两周后发生的，在此期间，财政部没有表示正在考虑改变回购计划。

西蒙斯写道：“这打破了财政部长期以来发布‘定期和可预测’公告的策略，并利用退款来宣布几乎所有的政策变化和指导。” “我们认为，说这种沟通策略的中断降低了他们指导的整体可信度并不夸张。”

此外，西蒙斯补充说，“发布的标题的草率措辞给人的印象是这是一个仓促做出的决定。”

那么，贝森特面临的挑战可能是，抑制长期收益率的努力可能会给投资者提供另一个要求更多补偿的理由。

贝森特周四对 CNBC 表示，并非所有起作用的因素都是根本性的。其中包括公司债券发行的竞争日益激烈，以及包括日本在内的其他主权国家的收益率突然变得有吸引力；与油价的相关性反过来又会增加人们对通胀的担忧；以及不断增加的期限溢价，或者投资者要求的额外收益。

为了解决这些问题，贝森特可以寻求与美联储的合作。尽管美联储主席凯文·沃什强调了让市场决定利率的重要性，但贝森特周四表示，这两个实体将“共同努力”应对债券市场的复杂情况以及美联储管理自己的国债持有情况。

在美国和全球政府债务市场的范式转变期间出现了各种变化。

穆迪评级首席信贷官Atsi Sheth表示：“美国政府债券的购买者也发生了结构性转变。” “随着各国央行缩减资产负债表，传统久期买家达到了他们能够吸收的额外发行量的极限，新买家，例如运行相对价值策略的杠杆对冲基金，正在发挥更大的作用。”

最重要的是，美国面临着严峻的财政形势，赤字与 GDP 之比接近 6%，约为二战结束至新冠疫情期间平均水平的三倍。这使得刚刚超过 40 万亿美元的国家债务问题变得更加复杂。

由于唐纳德·特朗普总统渴望减税，而国会几乎没有显示出限制支出的迹象，财政问题可能会加剧。为此，贝森特表示，他和管理和预算办公室主任拉塞尔·沃特(Russell Vought)将很快会面，讨论“财政整顿”，通常被理解为指减少赤字的努力。

BondBloxx高级投资策略师乔安妮·比安科(JoAnne Bianco)表示，“这是赤字、借贷需求、通胀预期、不真正了解美联储未来政策、以及能够发行越来越高水平的美国国债的可持续性以及这些利率需要达到的水平的综合因素。” “只是认为所有发行都需要更高的风险溢价。”
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
